title: Pashinyan says Armenia has frozen its participation in the CSTO
body:
On 22 February 2024 Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told France 24 that Armenia had frozen its membership in the Russian-led Collective Security Treaty Organization. RFE/RL published its report on 23 February. Pashinyan cited Moscow's months-long public calls for Armenians to topple his government and a propaganda campaign against him that he said had not let up. His government had long faulted the CSTO for failing to respond to the security challenges facing Armenia.

Armenian authorities blamed Russian peacekeepers, deployed to Nagorno-Karabakh in 2020, for not stopping Azerbaijan's September 2023 offensive. Moscow rejected the accusation, saying its troops lacked a mandate to intervene, and accused Pashinyan of paving the way for the collapse of separatist rule by recognising Azerbaijani sovereignty over the region. In November 2023 Pashinyan had skipped a CSTO summit in Minsk and said Armenia's membership would depend on its own state interests.

Pashinyan also claimed that Azerbaijan views Armenia as Western Azerbaijan and plans to attack and seize more Armenian territory. Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry called those claims unfounded in a statement on 23 February, saying they were meant to undermine the peace process. Asked about closing Russia's military base in Gyumri, Pashinyan said the issue was not currently on the agenda.
